recipes.name: Ice Cream Lasagna
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) jar crunchy peanut butter, divided
1 (3.9 ounce) package instant chocolate pudding mix
1 (16 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed
1 (12 ounce) jar hot fudge ice cream topping, divided
1 (12 ounce) jar caramel ice cream topping, divided

steps.text: Line the bottom of a 9x13-inch pan with 12 ice cream sandwiches.

Open the jar of peanut butter, place into microwave oven and microwave on low power for about 30 seconds at a time, until peanut butter is warm and spreads easily. Spread half the peanut butter over the layer of ice cream sandwiches.
Mix instant chocolate pudding mix into whipped topping; spread half the mixture over peanut butter layer.
Spread half the peanut butter cups over whipped topping layer.

Remove tops of hot fudge and caramel topping jars and microwave on low power for about 10 seconds at a time, just until toppings are warmed and liquid. Drizzle half of the fudge and caramel sauces over peanut butter cups.
Repeat layers, starting with remaining ice cream sandwiches, followed by remaining peanut butter, whipped topping mix, peanut butter cups, hot fudge sauce, and caramel sauce.
Freeze dessert until solidly frozen, 1 to 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Ice Cream Lasagna
raw_recipe.description: This yummy, chocolatey, peanut buttery, frozen layered ice cream lasagna treat is sure to be a hit with everyone at your next party or event!

video.description: Gooey, syrupy, chocolaty and peanut buttery, this ice cream treat ticks off all your essential dessert cravings and delivers the goodies one blissful bite at a time! The sweet layers begin by spreading peanut butter over a layer of ice cream sandwiches inside a baking pan. Then combine chocolate pudding mix and whipped topping to create a heavenly mousse and spread that on. Then add chopped peanut butter cups and generous drizzles of hot fudge and caramel sauces. Repeat all the layers, freeze and eat!

review.reviewBody: Very good. I have to admit to some tweaking . . . I used mini ice cream sandwiches - one layer - my 9x13 did not have room for a second layer. I also cut the sandwiches to fit the pan. I did not bother with the chocolate pudding mix in the Cool Whip - and it was not missed - at all. I used nearly 2x the peanut butter called for (in 2 layers), all the hot fudge and caramel sauce (one layer, each), and mini Reese's cups (one layer). I did the first layers as called for (not measuring the peanut butter), then, as I saw I was running out of room, I did another layer of peanut butter and topped with the last layer of Cool Whip. This got raves at a rehearsal dinner (= [I put it in the fridge when we started serving dinner, so it would soften a bit, after reading Frauline's note.] Oh! It took one box and a few extra of the mini sandwiches for the single layer - 18 mini's to a box . . .

My family loved this! After following the recipe exactly, I have a few suggestions: This makes two thick layers, so be sure to use a deep dish to prepare it. Mix your pudding mix and whipped topping together and chop your peanut butter cups before pulling your ice cream sandwiches out of the freezer. I did everything in the order listed and my ice cream sandwiches ended up starting to melt, so everything had to go back into the freezer to firm back up before I could proceed with the recipe. I used full-sized peanut butter cups as I could easily stack and chop them to a smaller size for better coverage over the two layers. If you do the same, I would recommend putting them in the freezer for about 15-20 minutes before chopping. At room temperature, the peanut butter portion of the cups tended to clump up a bit. I would recommend using an 18-ounce jar of peanut butter. I was barely able to cover the second layer -- I think 2 extra ounces would have been perfect. Regarding the peanut butter: I carefully removed the cardboard/foil top from the jar before microwaving, but there was a tiny bit of foil left along one edge that I didn't notice. It ended up starting a little fire in my microwave. I was right there and quickly turned it off, but would recommend carefully checking the rim of your jar to be sure no tiny fragments of foil remain before microwaving. Finally -- if your family enjoys this as much as my family did, it's sure to become a recipe you'll make time and again. I'm thinking I might try switching out the peanut butter cups for sliced bananas and a strawberry garnish next time for a banana split ice cream cake.. :)
This was excellent but very sweet. I cut it before freezing for easier serving just refrigerate for a bit, cut and freeze

Instead of dealing with preparing peanut butter cups, I chose to use Reese's flavored choc syrup, the "Magic shell" kind. It added more texture and stability to my lasagna!
Of COURSE we're making this again! My 8yo son did most of the layering.
Great idea, I scaled mine down and used mini ice cream sandwiches. Topped with peanut butter m&ms and mini peanut butter cups.

I made this exactly as the recipe was written. I should've thought ahead and used a deep Pampered Chef stoneware 9 x 13 I have for it spilled over the sides after adding the second layer to my regular Pyrex dish. This was a big hit for a birthday party. I was told by my girlfriend that she fell even more love with me after she ate this. Lots of lip smacking and yum yum noises from around the table.

This was so easy, and perfect for a child who does not like cake, for his birthday "cake", we put candles in it, and everyone enjoyed it! I used magic shell but no caramel, on 1 layer i usedeopolital ice cream sandwiches, and the other just vanilla to give it a colorfull look.
We loved this but it's HUGE. Next time I make it I will only do half the layers or make a smaller pan. It's delicious!
When I told my in-laws that I was fixing ice cream lasagna, they all went ewwww! After they had it, they all went WOW!
very easy and a great desert for a party!
Very easy recipe to follow and make. Really enjoyed making it with my children and they absolutely loved it!
This was a huge hit with adults and kids at our NYE party. It was so easy and a great make ahead party dessert. I will definitely make this again.
Made it exactly as written. Wouldn't change a thing. It was fantastic. Already sharing the recipe. Real crowd pleaser.

I found this recipe very sweet but enjoyed it quite a lot :)
At first I was a little hesitant because I was told that it has a lot of calories, sugar and fat...But its so worth it as this is the yummiest sweet thing I have had in a long time!

It has good texture, a great consistency and the layers of Ice cream were very yummy when combined with the Ice cream sandwiches etc. This is probably one of the best recipes of ice cream lasagna I have tried out of many..(my first attempts were too hard or too soft or didn't set right etc)
My one recommendation is to add marshmallows and sprinkles to the layers as this A- Improves the taste a heck of a lot, and B- Makes the decorative half of ice cream lasagna better (Just in case people are coming over, Its for a party etc.)

This particular recipe I found is a little on the pricey side but DEFINITELY worth as it lasted for a loooooonngggg time, The only problem with that was that I had to keep freezing and refreezing it as I couldn't eat it all at once because I would've been violently sick... But if the servings were made on the smaller side I could handle eating it :)

Personally..All in all I think this is one of the best desserts ever made and rate it 69/5 Stars!! LOVE IT..LOVE IT..LOVE IT!!!! 
Great recipe,
Thank you so much for sharing it with us
